sections.h2: Which county bills my Sioux Falls property tax?
sections.html:
Most Sioux Falls parcels get their bill from Minnehaha County. Lincoln County's treasurer bills the properties on its side of town. The city has an estimated 213,748 residents (July 1, 2025) and is the seat of Minnehaha County.

Read the county name printed on your notice before dialing, because the two treasurer offices do not share records.

OfficePhoneUsed for
Minnehaha County Treasurer(605) 367-4211Bills, payments, delinquent tax questions
Minnehaha County Equalization(605) 367-4228Owner-occupancy and assessment questions
Minnehaha County Auditor(605) 367-4220Levies and budgets
Lincoln County Treasurer(605) 764-5701Parcels in the Lincoln County part of the city

Three offices touch every bill: Equalization appraises and assesses the property. The Auditor converts budgets approved by elected boards into tax amounts. The Treasurer mails statements and collects the money.

November 1 is the assessment date. Whatever shape the property is in that day sets the next year's value. Land is generally valued by front feet. Building value depends on quality, size, design, condition and extras, then the structure is depreciated. Routine maintenance does not raise an assessment, though a major addition can.

One mill equals one-tenth of a penny, which works out to $1 for every $1,000 of assessed value. The city, the county and the school district each set a separate levy. Parcel records are open to anyone, and a visit to the Minnehaha Equalization office to review yours costs nothing.

sections.h2: Payment dates, penalties and ways to pay
sections.html:
Minnehaha County treats January 1 as the due date. You may pay half by April 30 and half by October 31 without penalty, and any unpaid half goes delinquent on May 1 or November 1. Late money costs 10 percent a year, roughly 0.83333 percent each month.

  • If a deadline lands on a weekend or holiday, the last working day before it applies, and the counter closes the books at 4:45 p.m.
  • Drop-box and web payments count until midnight.
  • A credit card payment adds a convenience fee of 2.35 percent.
  • An online e-check needs 7 to 10 business days to post.
  • Paper checks must be in-state checks with your name and address pre-printed in the top left corner.
  • Early payment is not offered, so there is nothing to gain by paying ahead.

Delinquent accounts are off limits to the website. Phone the Treasurer's Office. Mail payments to 415 N. Dakota Ave., Sioux Falls, SD 57104, with the stub. Add a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt.

South Dakota taxes a home you live in at a lower rate, but nobody applies it for you. SDCL 10-13-40 has the owner file a certificate with the county director of equalization, swearing to ownership and to living in the dwelling as the main residence on the assessment date.

  • The certificate must be filed by March 15.
  • The state allows it on a single dwelling per owner.
  • Once granted, it continues until the house changes hands or its use changes.
  • A buyer qualifies by filing the certificate of value at transfer, or by applying between November 1 and March 15.
  • The county board of equalization hears disputes over the classification.

At a sale, a buyer who moves in after November 1 applies for the next year. The title company will show you how the current bill is divided.

New state laws slow valuation growth on owner-occupied homes and reduce the school levy. Three changes from the Department of Revenue reach Sioux Falls homeowners.

  • SB 216 (2025) limits yearly growth in owner-occupied valuation to 3 percent for each county, and limits growth in local property tax budgets to the same 3 percent. It starts with the 2026 assessment notices, affects taxes paid in 2027, and lasts five years.
  • SB 245 (2026) uses a 0.3 percent sales tax increase to fund schools and cut the owner-occupied school levy, with a one-time payment so every homeowner sees a lower school levy on the 2027 bill.
  • SB 96 (2026) allows a county to add a local sales tax of up to 0.5 percent, possibly after a public vote, and spend it on a credit for owner-occupied property.

For the Sioux Falls School District, the mil rate drops from $7.13 in 2026 to $5.36 in 2027, a 23 percent cut on a typical home. The legal notice is titled Notice of Tax Increase even though the school levy falls, so do not be alarmed by the wording.

A few programs cut or postpone tax for qualifying owner-occupants. Most want an application by April 1, and the county treasurer takes them.

  • Assessment Freeze for seniors and disabled owners: age 65 or older or legally disabled, with income limits, filed by April 1.
  • Homestead Exemption: defers payment until the property is sold, available at age 70 under SDCL 43-31-1, filed by April 1.
  • Disabled Veteran exemption: for the owner-occupied home of a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected condition, filed by November 1 with the Director of Equalization.

The City of Sioux Falls also refunds the municipal part of the tax to low-income elderly or disabled owner-occupants approved for the state freeze. The refund is up to $500, paid the year after approval, and residents do not apply to the city. Call the city or county for the current home-value limit. Lincoln County residents file with the Lincoln County treasurer.

sections.h2: If a Sioux Falls property tax goes unpaid
sections.html:
When South Dakota property tax goes unpaid it becomes a lien, and given enough time the county can take the house through a tax deed. State law lays out the sequence.

  1. Half the tax is delinquent on May 1 and the other half on November 1 if unpaid by October 31 (SDCL 10-21-23).
  2. Interest runs monthly from each delinquency date, at five-sixths of one percent per month.
  3. The treasurer may offer tax certificates at a public sale on the third Monday of December (SDCL 10-23-7), when the commissioners authorize it.
  4. A tax deed proceeding can start three years after the certificate sale and must finish within six years (SDCL 10-25-1).
  5. The holder serves notice of intention to take a tax deed, and the right to redeem ends 60 days after the affidavit of service is filed.

You can redeem at any point before a deed is issued. Tax liens rank first, and interest and penalties are not waived. The Treasurer at (605) 367-4211 can quote a payoff.

A tax balance seldom stops a sale, because it is settled out of the proceeds at closing. The deed needs a Certificate of Real Estate Value (PT 56) naming the price and parties, and the register of deeds will refuse the deed otherwise.

SDCL 43-4-21 creates the transfer fee, and Minnehaha County's schedule shows $1.00 per thousand of value plus $30.00 to record the deed. Anyone who used the Homestead Exemption repays the deferred taxes and interest from the sale.

In practice: get the payoff from the treasurer, hand it to the title company, and the county is paid from what you receive. Owners who are behind and want to avoid repairs or showings can sell to us. We buy Sioux Falls houses as-is, promise nothing on price in advance, and charge nothing if you say no.

faqs.q: When are Sioux Falls property taxes due?
faqs.a: The due date is January 1, and you have until April 30 for half and October 31 for the rest. Anything unpaid after those dates is delinquent from May 1 and November 1.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Sioux Falls property tax late?
faqs.a: The county charges 10 percent a year on late payments, which is about 0.83333 percent per month.

faqs.q: How do I get the owner-occupied rate on my Sioux Falls home?
faqs.a: Send the county director of equalization a certificate by March 15 saying you own the home and live in it on the assessment date. Someone who just bought files after the transfer, from November 1 to March 15.

faqs.q: Can I pay Minnehaha County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. The portal takes e-checks and Discover, Visa or Mastercard. Cards add 2.35 percent, and online payments take 7 to 10 business days to post. Delinquent accounts must pay another way.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Sioux Falls house if taxes are delinquent?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the tax and interest from your proceeds at closing, using a payoff figure from the Treasurer's Office.
